 Dwayne Johnson Takes Action to New Heights in ‘Skyscraper’
 MOVIE NEWS 
 November 12, 2026 
 By Ari Coine 
 Image Soure: Universal Pictures Home Entertainment 
 Getting himself into trouble in a movie is something Dwayne Johnson takes to a whole new level. Villains battled, natural disasters survived, and somehow he gets out of situations that would probably kill the rest of us.
 Skyscraper is a good example. Johnson tries to save his family from a burning skyscraper in Hong Kong in the 2018 movie. This is not your average office building, either. One of those massive towers that would make you nervous just looking down from the top.
 The movie is back on HBO Max now, giving anyone who missed it in theaters a chance to see what the excitement was about. Pretty wild stunts fill this one, along with a character who gave Johnson a challenge he had not faced in many earlier roles. Running through a burning building and beating up bad guys was not the whole job. Johnson needed to consider something else.
 Dwayne Johnson has made a career out of action movies 
 Millions of wrestling fans already knew Dwayne Johnson as The Rock long before he became a movie star. Professional wrestling to Hollywood was not exactly overnight success, but he eventually found his place in the movie business.
 The Scorpion King and The Rundown got things started. The Fast & Furious franchise came later, along with movies like San Andreas , Jumanji: Welcome to the Jungle , and Rampage . Fighting people and escaping disasters has not been his whole career, of course. Comedies and family movies gave him a chance to do something different, too.
 Still, he looks pretty comfortable in a big action movie, you have to admit. Skyscraper was certainly right up his alley. A towering building catches fire, bad guys run around causing trouble, and a father has to figure out how to rescue his family.
 The Towering Inferno and Die Hard getting together to make another movie, almost. Johnson was not playing quite the same type of hero we had grown used to seeing, though.
 Will Sawyer was a different role for Dwayne Johnson 
 Johnson plays Will Sawyer in Skyscraper , a former Marine and FBI Hostage Rescue Team leader who lost one of his legs during a rescue operation. Private security work came next for Sawyer, and Hong Kong is where he finds himself inspecting a skyscraper called The Pearl.
 The building catches fire, unfortunately, and Sawyer gets blamed for what happened. His wife and kids are trapped inside on top of that, leaving him to save his family while trying to prove he was not responsible. His wife, Sarah, is played by Neve Campbell , who is also doing everything she can to keep their children safe.
 Sawyer’s prosthetic leg made him different from Johnson’s other action characters. Johnson is not an amputee, so he had things to understand about the character before stepping in front of the camera. Losing a leg would have changed Sawyer’s life long before the movie’s events. That was not something to forget once the explosions started.
 How Sawyer would move, react, and handle dangerous situations also mattered. Those details counted when playing someone who had gone through such a major life change. Tough guys fill Johnson’s filmography, but this character had a different background. Sawyer could still handle himself, although more defined him than physical strength.
 Dwayne Johnson spoke when Skyscraper originally came out about preparing for the role and the thought he put into portraying Sawyer’s disability.
 Click on the media bar below to hear Dwayne Johnson discuss what went into playing Will Sawyer in Skyscraper . 
 https://www.hollywoodoutbreak.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Dwayne-johnson-playing-amputee.mp3 
 ‘Skyscraper’ gets another chance with HBO Max viewers 
 Skyscraper was directed by Rawson Marshall Thurber , who had previously worked with Johnson on Central Intelligence . The film reached theaters in July 2018, when Johnson seemed to be everywhere at the movies.
 You probably remember the crane scene if you have seen it already, that enormous jump toward the skyscraper. I do not know about you, but standing on the crane would be hard enough for me. Forget jumping off it!
 Nobody watches a movie like Skyscraper expecting every stunt to be possible, then again. That is part of the fun. Johnson is going to attempt something completely outrageous, you know it, and you want to see how he gets out of it.
 A fairly simple story sits underneath all the action, too. Sawyer wants to save his wife and children, willing to do whatever it takes to bring them home. Why he would risk his life is not hard to understand, even if most of us would never want to be in his shoes.
 Skyscraper streaming again gives people who missed it in 2018 another chance to check it out. Those who saw it years ago might enjoy revisiting a movie that gave Johnson something a little different to work with, too.
 Sawyer stands out looking back at his career, because Johnson had to think about how his character’s experiences affected him before the main action even began. Do not worry, though. Plenty of running, fighting, and saving people remains. It would not be much of a Dwayne Johnson action movie without those things.
 Skyscraper is now streaming on HBO Max and is also available on DVD, Blu-ray, 4K Ultra HD, and digital platforms.
